task: Make fresh release-unit successor reevaluation reproject stale child Development Plan metadata from the current canonical Plan/Atlas projection before any strict authorization check, then require a second exact-candidate strict PASS before release execution can proceed.

operationalIntelligence.problemStatement: Live bounded rehearsal replay job 112651631798 proved STALE resumability and dependency bootstrap closure, then failed inside fresh successor reevaluation because the persisted U01 child Development Plan envelope still contained scope metadata projected under an older Knowledge/Atlas/Plan policy. The candidate material scope was valid, but strict Plan Before Code rejected stale subsystem, negative-knowledge, guard-digest and semantic-route declarations before a fresh child transaction could be authorized.
observableOutcomes: Fresh successor reevaluation first produces a non-authorizing canonical projection on the exact candidate head and fresh current-main base.
The projection exposes one machine-readable child-plan projection envelope containing the current guard digest, scope sets, negative knowledge, PO instructions and semantic execution route.
The child Development Plan is reprojected only from that machine output; no error-string parsing or hard-coded rehearsal metadata is used.
Child plan digest and release-unit binding identity are recomputed after reprojection.
A second strict Plan Before Code --check runs on the reprojected exact candidate and only strict PASS can return a fresh successor manifest.
Missing projection fields, UNKNOWN route relationships, projection command failure or strict second-pass failure remains fail-closed and creates no child PR.
unresolvedRisks: Treating the first projection as authorization would bypass strict plan validation.
Reprojecting only some fields could leave hidden stale authority or knowledge declarations in the child plan.
Parsing human-readable failure messages would couple release authority to unstable diagnostics.
Changing child plan digest without refreshing manifest/binding identity would break exact transaction identity.
A projection route with no proof obligation could still fail the current critical child execution contract.

in: Expose the canonical current plan projection envelope in Plan Before Code report output.
Add a release-unit child-plan reprojection helper that updates only projection-derived scope/route metadata and recomputes child plan and manifest binding identity.
Split successor reevaluation into dependency bootstrap, non-authorizing projection, reprojection, then strict Plan check on the same exact candidate worktree.
Preserve scrubbed GitHub credentials for both projection and strict proof subprocesses.
Add positive and fail-closed regression coverage for stale child metadata, projection identity and strict second-pass authority.
out: No manual child-plan field constants tied to this rehearsal.
No parsing of stderr issue strings as authoritative metadata.
No weakening of Plan Before Code, Atlas, Release Risk, CAS, PR, merge, Truth or Lifecycle authority.
No direct persisted release-state edit, blocker deletion, child PR creation or receipt fabrication.
No storefront, database, auth, payment, inventory, Builder, template or deployment change.

assuranceCeiling.rationale: This repair changes the trusted release executor's pre-authorization evidence refresh path. It must distinguish projection from authorization and preserve exact transaction identity across a current-policy reprojection.

acceptanceCriteria: Plan Before Code report emits a deterministic canonical child projection derived from the same projected files, Atlas, scope, Knowledge and execution-route computation used by its strict gate.

Projection includes guardDigest, expectedSubsystems, expectedDomains, expectedAuthorities, expectedKnownFailureIds, acknowledgedPoInstructionIds, acknowledgedNegativeKnowledgeIds and semanticExecutionRoute.
Successor reevaluation runs projection without --check only as data production; that result alone cannot authorize or return PASS.
Child reprojection refreshes plan metadata and recomputes child planDigest plus manifest/binding identity before strict validation.
Strict Plan Before Code --check runs after reprojection on the same candidate head and fresh current-main base; only strict PASS continues.
Projection missing required fields, route UNKNOWN, dependency failure, reprojection identity failure or strict failure remains RELEASE_UNIT_SUCCESSOR_REEVALUATION_BLOCK.
Exact-head CI, Completion Truth and Lifecycle close before merge; unchanged rehearsal then resumes from persisted state d4720b3689833facc40ae27a56094880279e42ba.
invariants: Projection is evidence input, never authorization.
No child manifest is authorized with stale plan projection metadata.
No scope metadata is derived from diagnostic text.
Reprojected child plan remains bound to the same releaseUnitId, parentTransactionId, intended files and fresh target base.
Plan digest, manifest digest, operation digest and binding digest remain internally consistent after reprojection.
Both projection and strict proof subprocesses execute with GH_TOKEN and GITHUB_TOKEN scrubbed.

failureModes: Old child plan blocks before current scope can be adopted.
Projection report omits one metadata family required by strict Plan validation.
Reprojection changes planDigest but manifest/binding digest remains stale.
Projection and strict pass accidentally run against different candidate heads or bases.
First projection fails to execute or emits malformed/non-canonical data.
Strict second pass still blocks because canonical route proof is incomplete.
edgeCases: Child intended files are unchanged but Knowledge applicability expands.
Current Plan policy changes guard digest without material source scope change.
A critical child consists only of added fixture files and requires a non-empty proof route.
Fresh successor is U02/U03 after predecessor main changes.
Projection succeeds but strict second pass detects real semantic UNKNOWN or obligation drift.

alternatives.summary: Run current Plan projection as non-authorizing data, reproject child plan from its machine envelope, then run strict Plan validation.
alternatives.reason: Reuses the canonical Plan computation while preserving an explicit authorization boundary.

alternatives.summary: Parse DEV_PLAN_* error messages and patch only failing fields.
alternatives.reason: Diagnostics are not an authority contract and this would miss silent stale fields.

alternatives.summary: Grandfather persisted child plan metadata after parent source admission.
alternatives.reason: Would defeat fresh successor reevaluation when Knowledge/Atlas/Plan policy evolves.

alternatives.summary: Patch the rehearsal U01 plan/state directly.
alternatives.reason: Would solve one fixture but invalidate the generic production-like rehearsal and bypass canonical state authority.

specialistReviews.finding: The missing edge is projection freshness between persistent release-unit manifests and an evolving Control Plane policy, not release-unit material decomposition.
specialistReviews.resolution: Make current Plan projection an explicit machine contract and refresh child plan metadata before strict authorization.

specialistReviews.finding: A non-check Plan run could be mistaken for an authorization result and silently weaken the release boundary.
specialistReviews.resolution: Label projection as non-authorizing, require a separate strict --check after reprojection, and expose no path that returns PASS from projection alone.

specialistReviews.finding: Child plan identity changes during reprojection, so all downstream manifest and binding identities must be refreshed before materialization or PR creation.
specialistReviews.resolution: Centralize reprojection in release-unit runtime and recompute child planDigest through refreshReleaseUnitIdentity before authorization.

specialistReviews.finding: The live rehearsal sequentially exposed dependency bootstrap, STALE recovery, then stale child-envelope freshness, proving the integration chain rather than isolated unit behavior.
specialistReviews.resolution: Add two-pass reprojection regression and replay the unchanged persisted rehearsal after merge.

challenge.scenario: The old child plan has a stale guardDigest but otherwise valid material scope.
challenge.finding: A single strict run blocks before the runtime can refresh metadata, so the executor cannot distinguish stale envelope from invalid material scope.
challenge.resolution: Run an explicitly non-authorizing projection first, consume only its structured canonical projection, then require a second strict check.

challenge.scenario: The projection report is BLOCK because declared metadata is stale.
challenge.finding: BLOCK diagnostics do not imply the projected scope computation itself is unavailable; however human error strings are not stable authority.
challenge.resolution: Emit the canonical projection fields as structured report data regardless of decision, and never parse diagnostic strings for reprojection.

challenge.scenario: Knowledge adds a newly applicable negative-knowledge rule while release-unit files remain unchanged.
challenge.finding: Persisted acknowledgedNegativeKnowledgeIds becomes stale without any material file drift.
challenge.resolution: Projection envelope carries the current negativeKnowledgeIds derived from current scope and the child plan replaces its acknowledgement set before strict check.

challenge.scenario: Current Atlas changes semantic route authority/proof requirements for the child.
challenge.finding: Keeping the old semanticExecutionRoute can either over-authorize or fail current critical route validation.
challenge.resolution: Projection envelope rebuilds route categories from the current execution skeleton and current architecture authority; strict pass remains the final validator.

challenge.scenario: Reprojection updates child planDigest but not bindingDigest or manifestDigest.
challenge.finding: PR context and Completion Truth could be bound to different transaction identities.
challenge.resolution: Use a runtime helper that recomputes child planDigest then refreshes release-unit identity and binding atomically before sealing/materialization.

challenge.scenario: Projection runs on candidate A but strict pass runs after candidate/base moved.
challenge.finding: Metadata could be authorized against a different exact state.
challenge.resolution: Both passes occur inside the same detached exact candidate worktree with fixed currentMainSha/candidateHead environment; any base drift remains blocked by normal reconciliation.

challenge.scenario: Projection envelope is incomplete or contains semantic UNKNOWN.
challenge.finding: Filling missing fields with old values would silently preserve stale authority.
challenge.resolution: Validate projection contract completeness and reject UNKNOWN/noncanonical projection fail-closed before rewriting the child plan.

challenge.scenario: Projection passes structurally but the reprojected child still violates current Plan policy.
challenge.finding: Projection freshness does not prove execution readiness.
challenge.resolution: Always rerun Plan Before Code with --check after reprojection; only that strict PASS can continue to fresh manifest authorization.

proofPlan: Commit this plan only and require Plan Before Code PASS before implementation.
Add structured canonical child projection output, child reprojection identity helper and two-pass successor reevaluation.
Add unit/regression tests for structured projection, digest refresh, token scrubbing, projection-not-authority and strict second-pass failure.
Require exact-head Knowledge, Plan, Edit-Time, Incremental Replay, Release Risk, full tests, TypeScript, build and Completion Truth PASS.
Commit only canonical lifecycle closure metadata and require final exact-head CI PASS.
Merge, verify fresh main CI, then rerun the unchanged bounded rehearsal from persisted STALE CAS state and accept only canonical U01 progression.

requirements.requirement: Fresh successor reevaluation must refresh stale child Development Plan projection metadata from current canonical machine evidence and still require an independent strict Plan PASS before authorization.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: A non-authorizing projection may not itself authorize a release unit.
A reprojected child plan may not retain stale plan or binding identity.
